purpose: Verified 2026 additions covering AMD RDNA 4 32GB professional GPUs and a current Ryzen AI 400 mini-PC. Vendor compute figures are retained as architecture metrics, not translated into tokens/second without reproducible LLM benchmarks.

software: llama.cpp via supported AMD GPU backends/runtime combinations
hardware.quantization_compatibility: Low-bit LLM formats are runtime-dependent. GGUF can be practical through llama.cpp-compatible AMD GPU paths; FP8/INT8/INT4 matrix peak figures are hardware capabilities and do not guarantee equivalent support in every LLM engine.

llm_suitability.practical_guidance: 32GB VRAM is well suited to many 20B-32B-class quantized models and can support selected larger heavily-quantized workloads depending on context/KV cache. The 640GB/s memory bandwidth at 150W is especially notable for autoregressive inference efficiency.

hardware.efficiency_notes: Using AMD reference specifications, 640GB/s at 150W yields about 4.27GB/s/W and 32GB at 150W yields about 4.69W per GB of VRAM. These are specification-derived ratios, not measured wall-power inference efficiency.

pricing.note: AMD has a live product page and current driver support, but a stable public retail price was not verified in this pass.

hardware.quantization_compatibility: Low-bit LLM support depends on ROCm/Vulkan engine implementation. Hardware FP8/INT8/INT4 matrix figures should not be treated as guaranteed performance for arbitrary GGUF/AWQ/GPTQ models.

llm_suitability.practical_guidance: The full 32GB VRAM pool is suitable for many 20B-32B-class quantized models. Compared with R9600, R9700S offers substantially more compute at the same 640GB/s memory bandwidth but doubles board power and requires server/workstation airflow.

hardware.efficiency_notes: The passive R9700S is primarily interesting for dense multi-GPU/server deployments. Its 640GB/s at 300W is about 2.13GB/s/W, roughly half the reference memory-bandwidth-per-watt ratio of R9600.

pricing.note: AMD exposes the product and current driver support, but no stable standalone public price was verified.

hardware.cpu: AMD Ryzen AI 9 HX 470, 12 cores / 24 threads
hardware.memory_note: AMD's processor specification supports up to 256GB, while the current MINISFORUM system specification advertises up to 128GB. The system limit is used for this product record.
hardware.storage: 3x M.2 2280 PCIe 4.0 NVMe; up to 12TB advertised total
software: Ryzen AI Software for NPU-compatible models
ROCm support is runtime/platform dependent and should be verified for Radeon 890M before deployment
hardware.quantization_compatibility: CPU/Vulkan local-LLM paths can use common low-bit GGUF formats when supported by the runtime. The 55-TOPS XDNA 2 NPU requires Ryzen AI-compatible model/operator workflows and should not be assumed to accelerate arbitrary GGUF models.

llm_suitability.practical_guidance: Up to 128GB replaceable DDR5 makes this useful for CPU/Vulkan experiments with models far larger than typical mini-PC soldered-memory systems. Large models may fit but decode speed is constrained by dual-channel DDR5 bandwidth; the NPU headline does not remove that limitation for arbitrary LLMs.

hardware.efficiency_notes: AMD specifies the HX 470 at 28W default TDP and 15-54W cTDP; MINISFORUM uses an internal 134.9W power supply. Supply rating is not measured wall consumption. Replaceable DDR5 and a low processor power range are useful for efficient always-on nodes, but independent LLM wall-power measurements are still needed.

pricing.note: MINISFORUM Canada displayed CA$1,040 sale pricing for the barebone configuration; stock state can vary by selector/session.
